nodes.text: Index cards in a rubber band gone brittle. Each has a date in the corner, each date in a different pen.

may day

fingers possessed wicked smile splitting my fat face
see how these teeth of mine shine
fangs buried deep in pink gums jaw locked tight
pieces of me crack snap pop old bones finding new foundation

flesh worried tight and anxious coiled in on itself
reptile hunger cold and waiting to strike
feel those swallowed whole brushing past displaced rib and spine
insect sense turned ultraviolet the sparkle of seed a sticky dust of life.
The tensile pull at the back of my neck feels like pulling on a pair of leather boots that are a size too small. Tiny bones shift and pop, tissue sponges and releases.

Winter Cactus.

A blind old cat calls out in early mid night.
Fingers peel back from grungied keys,
Snuck back away from a world away.

Fumbling over words, turned kept.
Half thought unfocused eternally dismissive.

Cold to the bone unheated home underthing shiver.
Movement scatters ambient chill, the peace of chattered calm.
Else prickled in a blanket, collapsed remembrance braced.

We walk through the house.
Loud noises punctuate our missteps.
Sometimes I encourage her exploration with rides or pets on head.
And whiskers prevent the majority of head on damage.
Tiny explosions pepper our outside and in.

The litter box is a negative.
Too late to eat again.
Hesitant to wander outside
at this strange cold hour.

I fluff the towel on her old chair
And pet until head lays down again.
Words come down to nothing. A transitional half-song of thought and human contact. We sing to ourselves, to our loved ones. Pay attention to the beat. That slow measure fever pitch of totality.
Listen to the human song. Birds became our dinosaur avian angels. Their lizard kin the serpent wrapped around our necks. What do we become.
“For the last year, I've written of inanimate objects & inanimate objects only. I've withheld the impulse to breathe life into these chunks of letter and word,

and going back to revisit long passages, I've furthered the study of these inarticulate and imaginary constructs, substance derived of only gentle repose, cast still life as full bodied word. In doing so, I've come to know the interior life of the void quite well.”
The last card is a different stock, heavier, and the date in its corner has been written over twice.
Dying for her was the easy part. Coming back, well, that was slightly harder.
The rubber band breaks when you try to put it back.
